data.headline: Average reserve balances rose as Treasury cash declined
data.summary: Average reserve balances reached $2.930088 trillion in the week ending November 4, up $36.318 billion from the week ending October 28. Average Treasury cash fell over the same comparison. These readings add funding context ahead of the market session. Their effect on lending, securities demand and risk appetite still depends on how institutions use the funds.

bull.text: Average reserve balances rose from $2.893770 trillion in the week ending October 28 to $2.930088 trillion in the week ending November 4, an increase of $36.318 billion.

Average Treasury General Account balances declined by $42.552 billion to $957.175 billion across those weeks. Separately, Wednesday Federal Reserve assets increased by $2.510 billion to $6.748145 trillion between October 28 and November 4.

bear.text: The ten-year Treasury yield was 4.90% on November 4, down 5 basis points from November 3. That benchmark remains a cost in financing and valuation calculations, whose other inputs can move independently.

watch.text: Overnight reverse-repo usage fell from $0.225 billion on November 4 to $0.125 billion on November 5. Keep this daily operation distinct from the weekly reserve and Treasury cash observations.
The October 27 S&P futures report shows asset managers net long 923,449 contracts and leveraged funds net short 400,604. These older category balances provide a separate positioning perspective.

limitations: Reserve balances and Treasury cash are week averages. Federal Reserve assets are Wednesday levels. These different measures cannot be added into a measured equity inflow or a complete causal explanation of reserve growth.
November 4 US observation dates precede the November 5 UK policy decision and the scheduled November 6 employment release. A response to either event remains unmeasured in these figures.
US ETF prices, premarket conditions, options, broad social coverage and calibrated outcome probabilities remain unavailable.
